refinedSections.summary: High-level overview of the trial design, objectives, patient population, endpoints, treatment schedule, and key study parameters for the Phase 1b/2a trial of Sym004 in combination with FOLFIRI.

refinedSections.title: 3. Background and Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Scientific and clinical context for the trial including disease background, current treatments, investigational product characteristics, trial rationale, and benefit/risk assessment.

refinedSections.title: 3.1 Disease and Treatment
refinedSections.summary: Overview of metastatic colorectal cancer epidemiology, staging, survival rates, and current treatment landscape including EGFR-targeted therapies.

refinedSections.title: 3.1.1 Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
refinedSections.summary: Epidemiology and survival statistics for colorectal cancer by stage, with focus on Stage IV metastatic disease (12% five-year survival).

refinedSections.title: 3.1.2 Current Treatment of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Disease
refinedSections.summary: Standard of care regimens including FOLFIRI, anti-EGFR antibodies (cetuximab, panitumumab), and RAS mutation status as a biomarker for treatment response.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 3.1.2 Current Treatment of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Disease

refinedSections.title: 3.2 Investigational Medicinal Product
refinedSections.summary: Description of Sym004 composition, mechanism of action, non-clinical findings, and summary of clinical safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy data.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.1 Sym004
refinedSections.summary: Sym004 is a 1:1 mixture of two chimeric IgG1 monoclonal antibodies (futuximab and modotuximab) targeting non-overlapping EGFR epitopes.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.2 Mechanism of Action
refinedSections.summary: Sym004 induces EGFR internalization and degradation through dual epitope binding, demonstrating superior activity versus single-agent anti-EGFR antibodies including in cetuximab-resistant cells.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.3 Summary of Non-clinical Findings
refinedSections.summary: In vitro and in vivo studies showing superior EGFR downregulation and anti-tumor activity versus cetuximab/panitumumab, with toxicology profile consistent with anti-EGFR class effects.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4 Summary of Clinical Findings
refinedSections.summary: Clinical experience with Sym004 across multiple tumor types including safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and antitumor efficacy data.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.1 Safety
refinedSections.summary: Safety profile from 175+ patients treated with Sym004 at various doses and schedules, documenting tolerability and adverse event patterns.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.2 Pharmacokinetics
refinedSections.summary: PK characteristics of Sym004 administration including dose-proportionality and exposure parameters.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.3 Pharmacodynamic Effects
refinedSections.summary: Biomarker and mechanistic assessments of Sym004 biological activity in clinical studies.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.4 Antitumor Effects
refinedSections.summary: Objective response rates and disease control observed with Sym004 monotherapy and combination therapy across tumor types.

refinedSections.title: 3.3 Trial Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Justification for evaluating Sym004 in combination with FOLFIRI in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer patients.

refinedSections.title: 3.4 Dose Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Scientific basis for starting dose selection and dose-escalation scheme based on prior clinical experience.

refinedSections.title: 3.5 Overall Benefit/Risk
refinedSections.summary: Assessment of potential benefits versus known and anticipated risks for trial participants.

refinedSections.title: 4. Trial Objectives and Endpoints
refinedSections.summary: Primary and secondary objectives for dose-escalation and dose-expansion phases, with corresponding endpoints for safety, efficacy, PK, and biomarker assessments.

refinedSections.title: 4.1 Dose-Escalation (Phase 1b)
refinedSections.summary: Objectives for the dose-escalation phase focused on determining maximum tolerated dose and recommended Phase 2 dose.

refinedSections.title: 4.1.1 Primary Objective
refinedSections.summary: To determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of Sym004 in combination with FOLFIRI.

refinedSections.title: 4.1.2 Secondary Objectives
refinedSections.summary: Assess safety, tolerability, antitumor activity, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of Sym004 plus FOLFIRI during dose-escalation.

refinedSections.title: 4.2 Dose-Expansion (Phase 2a)
refinedSections.summary: Objectives for dose-expansion phase evaluating antitumor activity and further safety characterization at the RP2D.

refinedSections.title: 4.2.1 Primary Objective
refinedSections.summary: To assess confirmed objective antitumor response to Sym004 at RP2D in combination with FOLFIRI.

refinedSections.title: 4.2.2 Secondary Objectives
refinedSections.summary: Further evaluate safety, tolerability, duration of response, progression-free survival, and overall survival during dose-expansion.

refinedSections.title: 4.3 Exploratory Studies
refinedSections.summary: Biomarker analyses including RAS mutation profiling, anti-drug antibodies, and other translational research endpoints.

refinedSections.title: 4.4 Trial Endpoints
refinedSections.summary: Detailed definitions of primary and secondary endpoints for both trial phases.

refinedSections.title: 4.4.1 Primary Endpoint of Dose-Escalation (Phase 1b)
refinedSections.summary: Occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) during Cycle 1 of Sym004 plus FOLFIRI administration.

refinedSections.title: 4.4.2 Primary Endpoint of Dose-Expansion Phase (Phase 2a)
refinedSections.summary: Confirmed objective antitumor response (complete or partial response) per RECIST v1.1 criteria.

refinedSections.summary: Detailed table listing all study procedures, assessments, and visits across the timeline of the study. Includes informed consent, eligibility criteria checks, demographics, physical examinations, medical history, pregnancy testing, laboratory tests, ECGs, vital signs, randomization, study intervention administration, genetic sampling, AE/SAE review, device deficiencies, concomitant medications, PK sampling, efficacy assessments, and PRO assessments with specific timing for each.

refinedSections.title: 2. Introduction
refinedSections.summary: Provides background context for the study including a brief description of the investigational intervention being studied. This section sets up the scientific and medical rationale for conducting the trial.

refinedSections.title: 2.1. Study Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Explains the scientific and clinical reasoning for conducting this particular study, including the unmet medical need, gaps in current knowledge, and how this study will address those gaps. Justifies why this research is necessary and timely.

refinedSections.title: 2.2. Background
refinedSections.summary: Provides detailed background information on the disease/condition being studied, the investigational intervention's mechanism of action, pharmacology, and prior research. References the investigator's brochure for comprehensive details on chemistry, efficacy, and safety data.

refinedSections.title: 2.3. Benefit/Risk Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive evaluation of the known and expected benefits versus risks of the investigational intervention. References additional documents like investigator's brochure, package insert, and development safety update reports for detailed safety information.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.1. Risk Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Detailed analysis of all potential risks associated with the investigational intervention and study procedures, including known adverse events, their frequency and severity, and risk mitigation strategies implemented in the protocol.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.2. Benefit Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Analysis of potential benefits to study participants and/or future patients, including anticipated therapeutic effects, contribution to scientific knowledge, and potential improvements in treatment outcomes.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.3. Overall Benefit Risk Conclusion
refinedSections.summary: Final determination that the anticipated benefits justify the identified risks for participants with the target indication, taking into account all risk minimization measures implemented in the study design.

refinedSections.title: 3. Objectives, Endpoints, and Estimands
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive table listing all study objectives (primary, secondary, tertiary/exploratory) with their corresponding endpoints, followed by detailed estimand specifications for each objective including population, endpoint, treatment condition, intercurrent events handling, and population-level summary measures.

refinedSections.title: 3.1. Estimand(s) for Primary Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Detailed specification of the primary estimand using ICH E9(R1) framework, including the clinical question of interest, target population, variable/endpoint, treatment condition, strategies for handling intercurrent events, and population-level summary. May include multiple primary estimands or coprimary estimands with rationale.

refinedSections.title: 3.1.1. Supplementary Estimand(s)
refinedSections.summary: Additional estimands that provide supplementary analyses for the primary objective using alternative strategies for handling intercurrent events or different population-level summaries. These support the primary estimand with sensitivity or alternative perspectives.

refinedSections.title: 3.2. Estimands for Secondary Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Detailed estimand specifications for each secondary objective, following the same ICH E9(R1) framework with clinical question, population, endpoint, treatment condition, intercurrent event strategies, and population-level summary. Each secondary objective may have its own estimand.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.1. Secondary estimand(s) for Secondary Objective [label]
refinedSections.summary: Specific estimand definition for a labeled secondary objective, including how discontinuation of intervention and rescue medications are handled (e.g., composite strategy, treatment policy strategy), and the population-level summary measure of interest.

refinedSections.title: 3.3. Estimands for [Tertiary/Exploratory/Other] Objectives
refinedSections.summary: Estimand specifications for exploratory or other objectives that are not primary or secondary. These may be less formally specified and may explore additional research questions or hypothesis-generating analyses.

refinedSections.title: 4. Study Design
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive description of the study design including overall design description, scientific rationale for design choices, patient input considerations, dose justification, and end-of-study definition. This section explains the fundamental structure and approach of the trial.

refinedSections.title: 4.1. Overall Design
refinedSections.summary: High-level description of the study design including intervention model (parallel, crossover, sequential, etc.), allocation method, blinding/masking approach, study phases, treatment groups, and overall study flow from screening through follow-up.

refinedSections.title: 4.2. Scientific Rationale for Study Design
refinedSections.summary: Justification for key design choices including selection of intervention model, comparator selection, study duration, visit frequency, and assessment timing. Explains why this particular design is optimal for answering the research questions.

refinedSections.title: 4.2.1. Patient Input into Design
refinedSections.summary: Description of how patient perspectives and feedback were incorporated into the study design. May include information about the optional Study Participant Feedback Questionnaire used to collect participant experience data to improve future trial design and conduct.

refinedSections.title: 4.3. Justification for Dose
refinedSections.summary: Rationale for the selected dose(s) or dose range, including supporting pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data, safety considerations, and dose-response information. For device studies, explains what constitutes a 'dose.' May include dose escalation/adjustment criteria and stopping rules based on safety or PK data.

refinedSections.title: 4.4. End-of-Study Definition
refinedSections.summary: Clear definition of when the study is considered complete (typically the last visit of the last participant or last scheduled procedure globally). Also defines what constitutes study completion for an individual participant (completion of all study periods and procedures).

refinedSections.title: 5. Study Population
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive section defining the target participant population including inclusion criteria, exclusion criteria, lifestyle restrictions, screen failure policies, and criteria for temporarily delaying enrollment or intervention administration. Begins with statement prohibiting protocol waivers.

refinedSections.title: 5.1. Inclusion Criteria
refinedSections.summary: Complete list of criteria that participants must meet to be eligible for the study, organized by categories including age, participant type and disease characteristics, weight and BMI, sex and contraceptive requirements, informed consent, and other study-specific criteria. All criteria must be met for enrollment.

refinedSections.title: 5.2. Exclusion Criteria
refinedSections.summary: Complete list of criteria that would disqualify a participant from the study, organized by categories including medical conditions, liver safety considerations, prior/concomitant therapy restrictions, prior/concurrent clinical study experience, diagnostic assessment findings, and other exclusion factors. Any single criterion met results in exclusion.

refinedSections.title: 5.3. Lifestyle Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Overall section covering lifestyle restrictions and requirements during the study including meals and dietary restrictions, caffeine/alcohol/tobacco limitations, activity restrictions, and other lifestyle constraints necessary for study integrity and participant safety.

refinedSections.title: 5.3.1. Meals and Dietary Restrictions
refinedSections.summary: Specific requirements for meals and dietary restrictions during the study, such as avoiding grapefruit juice, red wine, or specific foods that may interact with the intervention. May include fasting requirements and water restriction timing for food effect studies.

refinedSections.title: 5.3.2. Caffeine, Alcohol, and Tobacco
refinedSections.summary: Restrictions on caffeine/xanthine-containing products (coffee, tea, cola, chocolate), alcohol consumption, and tobacco/nicotine product use during dosing sessions or throughout the study. Specifies timing and duration of restrictions relative to dosing and sample collection.

refinedSections.title: 5.3.3. Activity
refinedSections.summary: Restrictions on physical activity and exercise during the study, such as abstaining from strenuous exercise before blood collection or clinical assessments. May allow light recreational activities while restricting vigorous exercise.

refinedSections.title: 5.3.4. Other Restrictions
refinedSections.summary: Any additional lifestyle restrictions or requirements not covered in previous subsections, such as restrictions on sun exposure, driving, occupational limitations, or other activities that may interfere with study procedures or safety.

refinedSections.title: 5.4. Screen Failures
refinedSections.summary: Definition of screen failure (participant consented but not enrolled), requirements for transparent reporting to meet CONSORT standards and regulatory queries, minimal data collection requirements (demographics, screen failure details, eligibility criteria, SAEs), and policies on rescreening with participant number assignment procedures.

refinedSections.title: 5.5. Criteria for Temporarily Delaying [Enrollment/Randomization/Administration of Study Intervention]
refinedSections.summary: Specific conditions or circumstances under which enrollment, randomization, or intervention administration should be temporarily delayed (e.g., acute illness, abnormal lab values requiring follow-up, intercurrent medical events) and criteria for when the participant can proceed.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 5.5. Criteria for Temporarily Delaying [Enrollment/Randomization/Administration of Study Intervention]

refinedSections.title: 6. Study Intervention(s) and Concomitant Therapy
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive section covering all aspects of study interventions including detailed description of interventions administered, rescue medications, medical devices, preparation and storage requirements, assignment/randomization procedures, blinding methods, compliance monitoring, dose modification rules, overdose management, and prior/concomitant therapy policies.

refinedSections.title: 6.1. Study Intervention(s) Administered
refinedSections.summary: Detailed tables describing all study interventions including intervention name, description, type (drug/device/biologic), dose formulation, unit dose strength, dosage levels, route of administration, use category (experimental/placebo/comparator), IMP/NIMP designation, sourcing, packaging and labeling, and current/former names. Also includes study arm descriptions.

refinedSections.title: 6.1.1. Rescue Medicine
refinedSections.summary: Description of permitted rescue medications including whether supplied by sponsor or obtained locally, specific rescue medications allowed, timing restrictions for rescue medication use relative to study intervention administration, and documentation requirements for rescue medication administration.

refinedSections.title: 6.1.2. Medical Devices
refinedSections.summary: List of all medical devices provided for the study including sponsor-manufactured devices and third-party devices, cross-reference to device use instructions, and requirements for documenting and reporting all device deficiencies (malfunction, use error, inadequate labeling) throughout the clinical investigation.

refinedSections.title: 6.2. Preparation, Handling, Storage, and Accountability
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for confirming appropriate storage conditions during transit, authorization for supply and administration, secure environmentally-controlled storage with limited access, investigator responsibility for accountability and record maintenance, and guidance for final disposition of unused study interventions.

refinedSections.title: 6.3. Assignment to Study Intervention
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for assigning participants to study intervention, with examples for IVRS/IWRS systems (central randomization with phone/web access) or precoded randomization provided to sites. Includes dispensing schedule, prohibition on redispensing returned intervention, and assignment documentation requirements.

refinedSections.title: 6.4. [Blinding, Masking]
refinedSections.summary: Description of blinding/masking approach for the study including who is blinded (participants, investigators, assessors), methods for maintaining blind (IVRS/IWRS, sealed envelopes, third-party dispensing), emergency unblinding procedures with investigator responsibility and sponsor notification requirements, and bias reduction strategies for open-label studies.

refinedSections.title: 6.5. Study Intervention Compliance
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for ensuring and documenting intervention compliance including double-checking for bulk supply preparation, direct observation for clinic dosing with mouth checks, documentation of date/time and dual verification, and compliance assessment methods for home administration (direct questioning, pill counts) with intervention accountability and reconciliation requirements.

refinedSections.title: 6.6. Dose Modification
refinedSections.summary: Procedures and criteria for dose reduction or modification when necessary due to tolerability or safety concerns. Includes description of modified dosing regimens or table of dose level changes to be implemented if dose adjustment is required.

refinedSections.title: 6.6.1. Retreatment Criteria
refinedSections.summary: Eligibility criteria that participants must meet to receive additional study intervention after initial treatment, determination process involving investigator judgment and participant agreement, and statement of whether retreatment will be blinded or unblinded.

refinedSections.title: 6.7. Continued Access to Study Intervention after the End of the Study
refinedSections.summary: Policies and procedures for providing continued access to study intervention for participants who complete the study and may benefit from ongoing treatment, including eligibility criteria, duration of continued access, and regulatory/ethical requirements for compassionate use or expanded access programs.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 6.7. Continued Access to Study Intervention after the End of the Study

refinedSections.title: 6.8. Treatment of Overdose
refinedSections.summary: Definition of what constitutes an overdose (e.g., exceeding specified daily dose within 24-hour period), availability or absence of specific antidote, and required actions for investigators including evaluation for intervention continuation, close monitoring for AEs and laboratory abnormalities, optional PK sampling, and documentation of excess dose quantity and duration.

refinedSections.title: 6.9. Prior and Concomitant Therapy
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for recording all medications and vaccines (prescription, over-the-counter, recreational drugs, vitamins, herbal supplements) with reason for use, dates, and dosage information. Includes washout requirements before study intervention, permitted medications (e.g., paracetamol/acetaminophen), and medical monitor consultation for questions about concomitant therapy.

refinedSections.title: 7. Discontinuation of Study Intervention and Participant Discontinuation/Withdrawal
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive section covering procedures for discontinuing study intervention (temporary or permanent) while remaining in study, participant withdrawal from the study entirely, and lost to follow-up procedures. Includes specific stopping criteria for liver events, QTc changes, and rechallenge policies.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 7. Discontinuation of Study Intervention and Participant Discontinuation/Withdrawal

refinedSections.title: 7.1. Discontinuation of Study Intervention
refinedSections.summary: Circumstances and procedures for permanent discontinuation of study intervention while participant remains in study for evaluations and follow-up. References Schedule of Activities for data collection at time of discontinuation and any further required evaluations.

refinedSections.title: 7.1.1. Liver Event Stopping Criteria
refinedSections.summary: Mandatory discontinuation criteria for abnormal liver tests including specific algorithm-defined conditions requiring intervention discontinuation, or investigator determination that discontinuation is in the participant's best interest based on liver chemistry abnormalities even if not meeting protocol-specified stopping rules.

refinedSections.title: 7.1.2. QTc Stopping Criteria
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for managing clinically significant ECG findings including QT interval changes (QTcB or QTcF), investigator determination of whether participant can continue study intervention, required documentation of ECG review, participant management changes, and reporting of clinically relevant findings as adverse events.

refinedSections.title: 7.1.3. Temporary Discontinuation
refinedSections.summary: Conditions and procedures for temporarily pausing study intervention administration with intention to resume, including criteria for when temporary discontinuation is appropriate, duration limits, monitoring during the pause, and criteria for safe resumption of intervention.

refinedSections.title: 7.1.4. Rechallenge
refinedSections.summary: Overall policies for restarting study intervention after stopping criteria are met, with specific subsection for liver chemistry rechallenge requiring sponsor board approval, ethics/IRB approval, separate consent, and participant education about risks of death, liver transplantation, hospitalization, and jaundice.

refinedSections.title: 7.2. Participant Discontinuation/Withdrawal from the Study
refinedSections.summary: Participant rights to withdraw at any time without consequences, investigator authority to withdraw participants for safety/behavioral/compliance reasons, requirement for early discontinuation visit per Schedule of Activities, procedures for handling withdrawal of consent for future information while retaining already-collected data, and participant request for sample destruction documentation.

refinedSections.title: 7.3. Lost to Follow up
refinedSections.summary: Definition of lost to follow-up (repeatedly fails to return and cannot be contacted), required contact attempts (3 phone calls, certified letter) before declaring lost to follow-up, documentation requirements, and optional procedures for vital status collection through public sources while maintaining legal and ethical boundaries.

refinedSections.title: 8. Study Assessments and Procedures
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive section detailing all study assessments including administrative procedures, efficacy/immunogenicity assessments, safety assessments (physical exams, vital signs, ECGs, laboratory tests, pregnancy testing, suicidality monitoring), adverse event reporting, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, genetics, biomarkers, immunogenicity, and health economics. Emphasizes adherence to Schedule of Activities and protocol waivers not allowed.

refinedSections.title: 8.1. Administrative [and General/Baseline] Procedures
refinedSections.summary: Administrative assessments and procedures including informed consent, participant identification assignment, screening procedures, baseline assessments, and general administrative documentation required throughout the study to ensure proper participant management and data collection.

refinedSections.title: 8.2. [Efficacy and/or Immunogenicity] Assessments
refinedSections.summary: Description of all efficacy and/or immunogenicity assessments specific to the study objectives, including measurement instruments, timing per Schedule of Activities, procedures for conducting assessments, and handling of assessment data to maintain blinding if applicable.

refinedSections.title: 8.3. Safety Assessments
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive safety monitoring section including physical examinations (complete and brief), vital signs measurements with specific procedures, electrocardiograms (single or triplicate), clinical laboratory tests with investigator review requirements, pregnancy testing, and suicidal ideation and behavior monitoring for CNS-active interventions.

refinedSections.title: 8.3.1. Physical Examinations
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for complete physical examination (cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, neurological systems minimum, plus height and weight) and brief physical examination (skin, lungs, cardiovascular, abdomen including liver and spleen). Investigators should pay special attention to signs related to previous serious illnesses.

refinedSections.title: 8.3.2. Vital Signs
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for vital signs measurement including temperature (with method specified), pulse rate, respiratory rate, and blood pressure. Requirements include 5-minute rest before measurement, automated devices preferred, blood pressure taken in triplicate at 1-minute intervals with average recorded, and participant position specified.

refinedSections.title: 8.3.3. Electrocardiograms
refinedSections.summary: ECG procedures including whether single or triplicate 12-lead ECGs will be obtained, timing per Schedule of Activities, automatic calculation of heart rate and intervals (PR, QRS, QT, QTc), and for triplicate ECGs requirement that 3 tracings be obtained in succession no more than 2 minutes apart. References QTc withdrawal criteria.

refinedSections.title: 8.3.4. Clinical Safety Laboratory Tests
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for protocol-specified laboratory tests per Appendix 2 and Schedule of Activities, investigator review and documentation of all results, recording of clinically significant changes as adverse events, procedures for repeating abnormal values until resolution or stabilization, etiology identification for persistent abnormalities, and requirements for local lab tests when needed.

refinedSections.title: 8.3.5. Pregnancy Testing
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for pregnancy testing in participants of childbearing potential, including test type (highly sensitive serum or urine hCG), timing per Schedule of Activities, and procedures for managing positive results. References Section 8.4.5 for pregnancy reporting and follow-up requirements.

refinedSections.title: 8.3.6. Suicidal Ideation and Behavior Risk Monitoring
refinedSections.summary: Monitoring requirements for CNS-active interventions or interventions with increased suicide risk, including baseline and ongoing assessment using specified scales, close observation especially at intervention start/end or dose changes, risk assessment for participants with signs of suicidal ideation/behavior, consideration of intervention discontinuation, and requirements to alert families/caregivers about monitoring needs.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.3.6. Suicidal Ideation and Behavior Risk Monitoring

refinedSections.title: 8.4. Adverse Events (AEs) Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), and Other Safety Reporting
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive AE/SAE reporting section covering definitions (Appendix 3/7), time periods and frequency for collection, detection methods, follow-up procedures, regulatory reporting requirements, pregnancy reporting, cardiovascular and death events, disease-related events, adverse events of special interest, and medical device deficiencies. Emphasizes investigator responsibility for detection, documentation, and follow-up.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4. Adverse Events (AEs) Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), and Other Safety Reporting

refinedSections.title: 8.4.1. Time Period and Frequency for Collecting AE and SAE Information
refinedSections.summary: Specifies collection period for SAEs (from consent or first dose until follow-up visit) and AEs (from consent or first dose until follow-up visit) per Schedule of Activities, requirement for immediate SAE reporting to sponsor within 24 hours, procedures for medical occurrences before intervention start, and investigator responsibility for reporting SAEs learned after study discharge if reasonably related to intervention.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4.1. Time Period and Frequency for Collecting AE and SAE Information

refinedSections.title: 8.4.2. Method of Detecting AEs and SAEs
refinedSections.summary: Emphasizes use of open-ended and nonleading verbal questioning of participants as the preferred method to detect adverse events and serious adverse events, avoiding introduction of bias in the detection process.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4.2. Method of Detecting AEs and SAEs

refinedSections.title: 8.4.3. Follow-up of AEs and SAEs
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for proactive follow-up of all SAEs and AEs of special interest until resolution, stabilization, event explained, or participant lost to follow-up. Investigator must follow participants at subsequent visits/contacts with additional follow-up procedures detailed in Appendix 3/7.

refinedSections.title: 8.4.4. Regulatory Reporting Requirements for SAEs
refinedSections.summary: Sponsor legal responsibility to notify regulatory authorities and other agencies about study intervention safety, compliance with country-specific safety reporting requirements to authorities, IRBs/IECs, and investigators. Investigator responsibilities to review and file safety reports, notify IRB/IEC per local requirements, and timelines for preparing and forwarding SUSARs (suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions) within 15 days.

refinedSections.title: 8.4.5. Pregnancy
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for collecting pregnancy information in participants and partners, reporting to sponsor within 24 hours, classification of pregnancy itself as not an AE/SAE but pregnancy complications and abnormal outcomes (spontaneous abortion, fetal death, stillbirth, congenital anomalies, ectopic pregnancy) as SAEs, follow-up of pregnancy outcome and neonate, and procedures for continuing or discontinuing intervention during pregnancy with required approvals and informed consent.

refinedSections.title: 8.4.6. Cardiovascular and Death Events
refinedSections.summary: Special procedures and requirements for reporting and following cardiovascular events and deaths that occur during the study, including adjudication processes, additional data collection, and regulatory reporting timelines specific to these serious events.

refinedSections.title: 8.4.7. Disease-related Events and/or Disease-related Outcomes Not Qualifying as AEs or SAEs
refinedSections.summary: Definition of disease-related events (DREs) common in the study population that typically won't be reported as SAEs even if meeting SAE criteria, monitoring by data/safety committee, and exceptions requiring AE/SAE reporting (if event is of greater intensity/frequency/duration than expected for the participant, or if investigator considers reasonable possibility of relationship to study intervention).
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4.7. Disease-related Events and/or Disease-related Outcomes Not Qualifying as AEs or SAEs

refinedSections.title: 8.4.8. Adverse Events of Special Interest
refinedSections.summary: Definition and listing of specific adverse events that are of particular interest for the study intervention or indication, requiring enhanced monitoring, follow-up, and reporting even if not meeting serious criteria. These events may have specific collection instruments or adjudication procedures.

refinedSections.title: 8.4.9. Medical Device Deficiencies
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for detection and documentation of device deficiencies (inadequacy in identity, quality, durability, reliability, safety, or performance) throughout all periods when medical device is used. Definition reference to Appendix 7, note that deficiencies meeting AE/SAE criteria follow those processes.

refinedSections.title: 8.4.9.1. Time Period for Detecting Medical Device Deficiencies
refinedSections.summary: Device deficiencies resulting in incidents detected, documented, and reported during all periods of medical device use. Investigator must promptly notify sponsor of deficiencies learned after participant discharge if reasonably related to study medical device.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4.9.1. Time Period for Detecting Medical Device Deficiencies

refinedSections.title: 8.4.9.2. Follow-up of Medical Device Deficiencies
refinedSections.summary: Follow-up applies to all participants including those who discontinue. Investigator responsible for supplemental investigations to elucidate nature and causality of deficiency. New or updated information recorded on original form with investigator signature and date.

refinedSections.title: 8.4.9.3. Prompt Reporting of Device Deficiencies to the Sponsor
refinedSections.summary: Device deficiencies reported to sponsor within 24 hours after investigator determines event meets protocol definition. Reporting method specified (e.g., electronic system) with alternative method identified. Sponsor contact designated for receipt of deficiency reports.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4.9.3. Prompt Reporting of Device Deficiencies to the Sponsor

refinedSections.title: 8.4.9.4. Regulatory Reporting Requirements for Device Deficiencies
refinedSections.summary: Investigator must promptly report all device deficiencies to enable sponsor fulfillment of legal responsibility to notify regulatory authorities and entities about medical device safety information. Investigator or responsible person complies with local regulatory requirements for reporting to IRB/IEC.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4.9.4. Regulatory Reporting Requirements for Device Deficiencies

refinedSections.title: 8.5. Pharmacokinetics
refinedSections.summary: Description of PK sampling including sample type (plasma/serum/whole blood/urine), volume, timing per Schedule of Activities, procedures for collection and handling, number of aliquots, potential for additional timepoint sampling based on emerging data, and confidentiality measures to maintain blinding. May state PK parameters not evaluated if not applicable.

refinedSections.title: 8.6. Pharmacodynamics
refinedSections.summary: Description of pharmacodynamic assessments and biomarkers that will be measured to evaluate the biological or physiological effects of the study intervention, including sample types, timing, procedures, and analysis plans for PD endpoints.

refinedSections.title: 8.7. Genetics
refinedSections.summary: Genetic sampling procedures including blood or saliva sample collection for DNA isolation from consenting participants (participation optional), volume, procedures for DNA extraction failure replacement, reference to Appendix 5 for detailed genetic research information, and collection/shipment/destruction processes. May state genetics not evaluated if not applicable.

refinedSections.title: 8.8. Biomarkers
refinedSections.summary: Description of biomarker sample collection (sample type, protocol-specific objectives, biomarker names), timing per Schedule of Activities and laboratory manual, storage duration (up to specified years), and optional further research use with participant consent for understanding disease, treatment development, or research methods. May state biomarkers not evaluated if not applicable.

refinedSections.title: 8.9. Immunogenicity Assessments
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for evaluating antibodies to study intervention in plasma/serum samples per Schedule of Activities and at final visit for discontinuing participants, screening for binding antibodies with titer reporting, neutralizing antibody characterization, validated assay methods, coordination with intervention concentration measurement, sample storage duration, and further antibody characterization analyses.

refinedSections.title: 8.10. [Health Economics OR Medical Resource Utilization and Health Economics]
refinedSections.summary: Collection of health care resource utilization data including reasons and duration of hospitalizations and emergency room visits (excluding protocol-mandated procedures and encounters). Sponsor may use collected data to conduct economic analyses. May state health economics not evaluated if not applicable.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.10. [Health Economics OR Medical Resource Utilization and Health Economics]

refinedSections.title: 9. Statistical Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive statistical section covering general considerations (decision criteria, multiplicity adjustment, intercurrent events, missing data), analysis sets definitions, analyses for primary/secondary/exploratory objectives, safety analyses, other analyses including subgroups, interim analyses, and sample size determination. Notes that statistical analysis plan will provide more detailed technical descriptions.

refinedSections.title: 9.1. General Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Overview of general statistical principles for the study including decision criteria/statistical hypotheses, multiplicity adjustment strategies, impact of intercurrent events, and handling of missing data. Provides foundation for all statistical analyses.

refinedSections.title: 9.1.1. [Decision Criteria/Statistical Hypotheses]
refinedSections.summary: Specification of nominal significance levels, one- or two-sided tests, confidence interval probabilities, and formal null and alternative hypotheses for primary and secondary objectives. May include superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence hypotheses with justification for non-inferiority margins. Defines statistical framework for hypothesis testing.

refinedSections.title: 9.1.2. Multiplicity Adjustment
refinedSections.summary: Strategy for controlling family-wise error rate across multiple comparisons, such as hierarchical testing procedures, closed testing procedures, alpha spending approaches, or fixed sequence testing. Ensures overall type I error rate maintained at specified level (e.g., 5%) when testing multiple hypotheses.

refinedSections.title: 9.1.3. Impact of Intercurrent Events Strategies
refinedSections.summary: Description of how intercurrent events (events occurring after treatment initiation that affect interpretation of the endpoint) will be handled in the analysis, aligned with the estimand framework. Strategies may include treatment policy, composite, hypothetical, while on treatment, or principal stratum approaches.

refinedSections.title: 9.1.4. Handling of Missing Data
refinedSections.summary: Approach for handling missing data in the analysis, including primary analysis method, sensitivity analyses to assess robustness, and assumptions about missingness mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR). May include multiple imputation, mixed models, or other methods appropriate for the data and estimand.

refinedSections.title: 9.2. Analysis Sets
refinedSections.summary: Definitions of all participant analysis sets (e.g., Full Analysis Set, Safety Analysis Set, Per Protocol Set) and data points sets used for different estimands and objectives. Specifies which participants and which data will be included in each analysis, treatment assignment principles (planned vs. actual), and alignment with estimands.

refinedSections.title: 9.3. Analyses Supporting Primary Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Detailed description of statistical analyses for the primary objective including endpoint definition, main analytical approach (statistical model, covariates, estimands), sensitivity analyses to assess robustness, and supplementary analyses to provide additional perspectives on the primary objective.

refinedSections.title: 9.3.1. Primary [Endpoint(s)/Estimand(s)]
refinedSections.summary: Subsection containing detailed specifications for primary endpoint(s) or estimand(s) including endpoint definition, main analytical approach with statistical methods, sensitivity analyses, and supplementary analyses.

refinedSections.title: 9.4. Analyses Supporting Secondary Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Statistical analyses for all secondary objectives, organized by objective with subsections for each. Describes analytical methods, models, and approaches for each secondary endpoint/estimand, recognizing hierarchical testing constraints from multiplicity adjustment.

refinedSections.title: 9.4.1. Analyses Supporting Secondary Objective [label]
refinedSections.summary: Specific analytical approach for a labeled secondary objective including statistical methods, models, covariates, and handling of intercurrent events consistent with the secondary estimand definition. Subject to hierarchical testing order from multiplicity adjustment.

refinedSections.title: 9.5. Analyses Supporting [Tertiary/Exploratory/Other] Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Statistical analyses for exploratory or other objectives not subject to formal hypothesis testing. These are typically descriptive or hypothesis-generating analyses without multiplicity adjustment, providing additional insights beyond primary and secondary objectives.

refinedSections.title: 9.6. [Other] Safety Analyses
refinedSections.summary: Description of safety data analyses including adverse events, serious adverse events, laboratory values, vital signs, ECGs, and other safety assessments. Typically descriptive summaries by treatment group with frequency tables, time to event analyses, and special analyses for safety topics of interest.

refinedSections.title: 9.7. Other Analyses
refinedSections.summary: Section covering additional analyses not fitting into primary, secondary, exploratory, or safety categories, including analyses of other variables/parameters and subgroup analyses.

refinedSections.title: 9.7.1. Other variables and/or parameters
refinedSections.summary: Analyses of additional variables or parameters such as demographics, baseline characteristics, protocol deviations, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, biomarkers, or other data not specifically addressed in other analysis sections.

refinedSections.title: 9.7.2. Subgroup analyses
refinedSections.summary: Prespecified analyses within subgroups of participants defined by baseline characteristics (e.g., age, sex, disease severity, geographic region) to explore consistency of treatment effects. Includes specification of subgroups and methods for subgroup comparisons, recognizing exploratory nature.

refinedSections.title: 9.8. Interim [Analysis/Analyses]
refinedSections.summary: Description of any planned interim analyses including purpose (efficacy monitoring, futility, sample size re-estimation), timing based on information fraction or events, analysis methods, alpha spending or decision boundaries, independent data monitoring committee role, unblinding procedures, and measures to maintain study integrity. Statistical analysis plan will provide greater detail.

refinedSections.title: 9.9. Sample Size Determination
refinedSections.summary: Justification for the planned sample size including target number of participants to enroll/randomize, basis for calculation (primary efficacy estimand/endpoint), assumptions about response rates or effect sizes, statistical test and significance level, desired power, and assumptions about intercurrent events and dropout. May include calculations for secondary objectives.

refinedSections.title: 10. Supporting Documentation and Operational Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Major section containing all appendices covering regulatory and ethical considerations, clinical laboratory tests, AE/SAE definitions and procedures, contraceptive guidance, genetics details, liver safety guidelines, medical device reporting procedures, country-specific requirements, and protocol amendment history.

refinedSections.title: 10.1. Appendix 1: Regulatory, Ethical, and Study Oversight Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive appendix covering regulatory and ethical requirements including compliance with Declaration of Helsinki, ICH GCP, and local laws; IRB/IEC submission and approval processes; financial disclosure; informed consent procedures; recruitment strategy; data protection; committee structures; dissemination of clinical data; data quality assurance; source documents; study/site start and closure; and publication policy.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.1. Appendix 1: Regulatory, Ethical, and Study Oversight Considerations

refinedSections.title: 10.1.1. Regulatory and Ethical Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for conducting study in accordance with Declaration of Helsinki, CIOMS guidelines, ICH GCP, and applicable laws and regulations. IRB/IEC submission and approval requirements for protocol, amendments, informed consent, and study documents. Health authority approval requirements. Investigator responsibilities for status reporting, SAE notification, and oversight.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.2. Financial Disclosure
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for investigators and sub-investigators to provide sufficient, accurate financial information to sponsor to enable complete and accurate financial certification or disclosure statements to regulatory authorities, documenting potential financial conflicts of interest.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.3. Informed Consent Process
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive informed consent procedures including investigator explanation of study nature, risks, and benefits; voluntary participation; signature requirements meeting 21 CFR 50, local regulations, ICH guidelines, and privacy laws; documentation in medical record; reconsent to current versions; providing copies to participants; rescreening consent requirements; optional exploratory research consent; pregnancy continuation consent; and two-step consent for complex studies.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.4. Recruitment strategy
refinedSections.summary: Description of the approach and methods for recruiting participants into the study, including identification of potential participants, recruitment materials and advertisements, outreach strategies, and any specific considerations for ensuring diverse and representative enrollment.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.5. Data Protection
refinedSections.summary: Participant privacy and data protection measures including unique identifier assignment, no transfer of identifying information to sponsor, participant informed about data use in accordance with local data protection law and consent requirements, medical record examination by auditors and regulators, contractual data protection responsibilities, and information technology security measures against unauthorized disclosure or access.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.6. Committees Structure
refinedSections.summary: Description of study oversight committees including data monitoring committees, safety review committees, and adjudication committees. Covers composition, responsibilities, meeting frequency, and decision-making authority. Includes subsection on early safety data review procedures.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.6.1. [Early Safety Data Review AND/OR Committee]
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for continuous safety monitoring by sponsor internal/external safety review committee, early aggregated safety data review for initial participants (stepwise approach), specification of events that would trigger study pause/stop (deaths, SAEs, specific adverse events exceeding thresholds), decision process for resumption, and case unblinding procedures if necessary.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.7. Dissemination of Clinical Study Data
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for providing study participants the option of receiving their individual study data, with management and processes described in study data management or individual participant data return plan in accordance with sponsor policies, laws, and regulations.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.8. Data Quality Assurance
refinedSections.summary: Data quality procedures including investigator responsibility for accurate CRF completion and signature, CRF completion guidance location, requirements for monitoring, audits, IRB/IEC review, and regulatory inspections with direct access to source documents, quality tolerance limits for identifying systematic issues, monitoring plan details (risk-based approaches, central/remote/on-site monitoring), sponsor data management responsibility, accountability for delegated actions, and record retention requirements.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.9. Source Documents
refinedSections.summary: Requirements for source documents that provide evidence of participant existence and data integrity, filing at investigator site, consistency between CRF entries and source documents or documented discrepancies, requesting previous medical records, maintaining accurate source documentation, definition of source data and origin, and monitoring to confirm accuracy, completeness, and verifiability from source documents.

refinedSections.title: 10.1.10. Study and Site Start and Closure
refinedSections.summary: Study start date definition (date open for recruitment), first act of recruitment definition (first site open or other), study/site termination procedures with sponsor and investigator authority, reasons for early closure (development discontinuation, protocol non-compliance, inadequate recruitment, target enrollment reached), site closure definition (when documents/supplies collected and closure visit performed), and requirements for notifying investigators, IRBs, authorities, and participants of premature termination/suspension with appropriate therapy and follow-up.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.1.10. Study and Site Start and Closure

refinedSections.title: 10.1.11. Publication Policy
refinedSections.summary: Publication policies including sponsor rights to review manuscripts/abstracts before submission to protect proprietary information and provide comments, compliance with publication requirements, support for multicenter study publication in entirety rather than individual site data with coordinating investigator designation, and authorship determination by mutual agreement following International Committee of Medical Journal Editors requirements.

refinedSections.title: 10.2. Appendix 2: Clinical Laboratory Tests
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive appendix detailing all protocol-required laboratory tests including hematology (platelet count, RBC count and indices, reticulocytes, WBC differential, hemoglobin, hematocrit), clinical chemistry (BUN, creatinine, electrolytes, glucose, liver function tests, bilirubin, protein), routine urinalysis (specific gravity, pH, dipstick, microscopy), pregnancy testing (hCG), other screening tests (FSH, estradiol, drug/alcohol screen, serology for HIV/hepatitis), investigator review requirements, and liver chemistry stopping criteria notes.

refinedSections.title: 10.3. Appendix 3: AEs and SAEs: Definitions and Procedures for Recording, Evaluating, Follow-up, and Reporting
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive appendix defining adverse events (untoward medical occurrence temporally associated with intervention) and serious adverse events (results in death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or other important medical events), distinguishing unsolicited vs. solicited AEs, specifying events meeting and not meeting AE definition, providing intensity assessment criteria (mild/moderate/severe), causality assessment guidance (reasonable possibility), and procedures for recording, follow-up, and reporting AEs/SAEs to sponsor via electronic or paper data collection tools within specified timeframes.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.3. Appendix 3: AEs and SAEs: Definitions and Procedures for Recording, Evaluating, Follow-up, and Reporting

refinedSections.title: 10.3.1. Definition of AE
refinedSections.summary: Detailed definition of adverse event as any untoward medical occurrence temporally associated with study intervention regardless of causality, including distinction between unsolicited AEs (spontaneously reported) and solicited AEs (predefined events participant specifically questioned about in diary), and comprehensive lists of events meeting the AE definition (abnormal labs, disease exacerbation, new conditions, drug interactions, overdose sequelae) and events not meeting the definition (underlying disease findings, expected disease progression, procedures rather than conditions, social admissions, anticipated fluctuations).

refinedSections.title: 10.3.2. Definition of SAE
refinedSections.summary: Detailed definition of serious adverse event as untoward medical occurrence meeting one or more criteria: results in death; is life-threatening (participant at risk of death at time of event); requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization (with notes on elective procedures); results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity (substantial disruption of normal life functions); is congenital anomaly/birth defect; is suspected transmission of infectious agent via authorized medicinal product; or other important medical events requiring medical judgment (invasive cancers, intensive emergency treatment, blood dyscrasias, convulsions, intervention dependency/abuse).

refinedSections.title: 10.3.3. Recording and Follow-Up of AE and/or SAE
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for AE/SAE recording including investigator review of all documentation (hospital notes, lab reports, diagnostics), recording on appropriate forms (not photocopies of medical records unless requested by sponsor with participant identifiers redacted), establishing diagnosis rather than individual signs/symptoms when possible, intensity assessment (mild/moderate/severe with detailed definitions), causality assessment using clinical judgment considering reasonable possibility and alternative causes, and follow-up requirements including supplemental investigations, postmortem findings if applicable, recording updated information on original documents, and submitting updated SAE data to sponsor within 24 hours.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.3.3. Recording and Follow-Up of AE and/or SAE

refinedSections.title: 10.3.4. Reporting of SAEs
refinedSections.summary: SAE reporting procedures to sponsor via electronic data collection tool as primary mechanism (with paper backup if system unavailable), entry into electronic system as soon as available, procedures after site completion when system offline (paper forms or telephone to medical monitor/SAE coordinator), and contacts for SAE reporting. For paper reporting, facsimile transmission preferred with overnight mail/courier backup, noting telephone notification doesn't replace completed signed SAE form within designated timeframes.

refinedSections.title: 10.4. Appendix 4: Contraceptive and Barrier Guidance
refinedSections.summary: Appendix providing definitions of contraceptive terms and detailed guidance on acceptable contraceptive methods for study participants, including requirements for participants of childbearing potential and their partners, timing of contraceptive use relative to study intervention, and barrier methods to prevent pregnancy and disease transmission during the study.

refinedSections.title: 10.5. Appendix 5: Genetics
refinedSections.summary: Detailed genetics research information including genetic variation impact on intervention response and disease, DNA sample use for research related to intervention and indication (candidate genes, genome-wide, or entire genome analysis), potential development of diagnostic tests, multi-study assessments, results reporting in CSR or separate summary, secure storage with confidentiality measures, and retention period while research continues (up to specified years or per local requirements).

refinedSections.title: 10.6. Appendix 6: Liver Safety: Suggestions and Guidelines for Liver Events
refinedSections.summary: Appendix providing detailed liver safety monitoring guidance including liver chemistry stopping criteria algorithms, management of participants meeting liver stopping criteria, follow-up requirements, rechallenge procedures if permitted, and specific monitoring for drug-induced liver injury (DILI) including Hy's Law criteria.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.6. Appendix 6: Liver Safety: Suggestions and Guidelines for Liver Events

refinedSections.title: 10.7. Appendix 7: Medical Device AEs, ADEs, SAEs, SADEs, USADEs and Device Deficiencies: Definitions and Procedures for Recording, Evaluating, Follow-up, and Reporting in Medical Device Studies
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive appendix for medical device studies compliant with ISO 14155 and EU MDR 2017/745, defining medical device AE (untoward occurrence in participant, users, or other persons temporally associated with device use) and ADE (adverse device effect related to device use), SAE/SADE/USADE definitions with device-specific criteria, device deficiency definition (inadequacy in identity, quality, durability, reliability, safety, or performance including malfunctions, use errors, inadequate information), and procedures for recording, intensity assessment, causality assessment, follow-up, and reporting to sponsor via electronic or paper systems within 24 hours, including special requirements for device deficiencies potentially related to SAEs.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.7. Appendix 7: Medical Device AEs, ADEs, SAEs, SADEs, USADEs and Device Deficiencies: Definitions and Procedures for Recording, Evaluating, Follow-up, and Reporting in Medical Device Studies

refinedSections.title: 10.7.1. Definition of Medical Device AE and ADE
refinedSections.summary: Medical device AE defined as any untoward medical occurrence in participant, users, or other persons temporally associated with device use (including events related to investigational device, comparator, and procedures, with note that events in users/other persons only include device-related events). ADE defined as AE related to device use including events from insufficient instructions, deployment issues, malfunction, use error, or intentional misuse.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.7.1. Definition of Medical Device AE and ADE

refinedSections.title: 10.7.2. Definition of Medical Device SAE, SADE and USADE
refinedSections.summary: Medical Device SAE defined as serious event that led to death, serious health deterioration (life-threatening illness/injury, permanent impairment, inpatient/prolonged hospitalization, medical/surgical intervention to prevent serious outcome, chronic disease per MDR 2017/745), fetal distress/death/congenital abnormality, or suspected infectious agent transmission. SADE defined as adverse device effect resulting in SAE consequences or device deficiency that might have led to SAE if action not taken. USADE defined as serious adverse device effect not identified in current risk analysis report (also identified as UADE in 21 CFR 813.3).
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.7.2. Definition of Medical Device SAE, SADE and USADE

refinedSections.title: 10.7.3. Definition of Device Deficiency
refinedSections.summary: Device deficiency defined as inadequacy of medical device with respect to its identity, quality, durability, reliability, safety, or performance. Includes malfunctions, use errors, and inadequacy of manufacturer-supplied information.

refinedSections.title: 10.7.4. Recording and Follow-Up of Medical Device AE and/or SAE and Device Deficiencies
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for recording device-related AE/SAE/deficiency including investigator review of all documentation, recording in medical records and appropriate forms (not photocopies of medical records unless requested), establishing diagnosis when possible, describing corrective/remedial actions for deficiencies, intensity assessment (mild/moderate/severe), causality assessment using clinical judgment, investigator review and causality documentation before initial transmission, ability to update causality in light of follow-up information, and follow-up requirements including supplemental investigations, postmortem findings, recording updated information with signature/date, and submitting updated SAE data to sponsor within 24 hours.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.7.4. Recording and Follow-Up of Medical Device AE and/or SAE and Device Deficiencies

refinedSections.title: 10.7.5. Reporting of Medical Device SAEs
refinedSections.summary: Medical device SAE reporting to sponsor via electronic data collection tool as primary mechanism (with paper backup if unavailable), entry into electronic system when available, procedures after site completion when system offline (paper forms or telephone to medical monitor/SAE coordinator), and reporting contacts. Paper reporting via facsimile transmission preferred with overnight mail/courier backup, noting telephone notification doesn't replace completed signed SAE form within designated timeframes.

refinedSections.title: 10.7.6. Reporting of SADEs
refinedSections.summary: SADE reporting with note of additional obligations for device deficiencies potentially related to SAEs to notify regulatory authorities and entities. Any device deficiency associated with SAE reported to sponsor within 24 hours after investigator determines event meets deficiency definition. Sponsor reviews all deficiencies, determines and documents in writing whether could have led to SAE, and reports to regulatory authorities and IRBs/IECs per national regulations.

refinedSections.title: 10.8. Appendix 8: Country-specific Requirements
refinedSections.summary: Appendix documenting any country-specific regulatory, ethical, or operational requirements that differ from the global protocol. Used for protocols implemented across multiple countries with varying local regulations and practices requiring protocol adaptations.

refinedSections.title: 10.9. Appendix 9: Protocol Amendment History
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive amendment history including reference to Protocol Amendment Summary of Changes Table before table of contents, for each amendment: amendment number, date, substantial/nonsubstantial designation per EU Regulation 536/2014, overall rationale, and detailed table of section number/name, description of change, and brief rationale. Includes examples of numbering conventions for global, country-specific, and site-specific amendments, and document history table examples showing all amendments and original protocol with dates.

refinedSections.title: 11. References
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive list of all references cited throughout the protocol including scientific literature, regulatory guidance documents, previous studies, investigator's brochure versions, and other supporting documentation. References formatted according to standard citation style (e.g., ICMJE format).
